strategic_objective: 1. Drive Sustainable Revenue Growth & Global Diversification
strategic_theme_alignment: Operational Excellence  |  Business Growth & Strategic Partnership  (Aligns to Corporate SO16 – Increase Revenue)
intended_result: A scalable, market-driven revenue engine that accelerates regional and international expansion, grows recurring subscription income, and diversifies revenue through partner and digital channels — delivering N$600 million in FY2026/27 and a ≥ 25% CAGR toward the 2030 ambition.
key_initiatives:
1.1  Approve and drive an annual Group sales plan with territory-specific revenue targets.
     ↳  Intended Result:  MD owns the revenue plan and holds EXCO to territory targets, anchoring the N$600m FY2026/27 goal.

1.2  Lead the SADC and international market-entry programme.
     ↳  Intended Result:  MD sequences and resources market entry country-by-country, steadily lifting the international revenue share.

1.3  Embed a SaaS, subscription-first commercial model across the portfolio.
     ↳  Intended Result:  MD shifts the commercial model toward recurring revenue, improving predictability, retention and valuation.

1.4  Grow channel-partner revenue contribution.
     ↳  Intended Result:  MD ties the partner programme to revenue targets so partners become a material, low-cost growth engine.

1.5  Launch e-commerce and self-service revenue streams.
     ↳  Intended Result:  MD prioritises a live digital channel so Green captures scalable, low-marginal-cost income from year two.

1.6  Review revenue performance and pipeline conversion monthly at EXCO.
     ↳  Intended Result:  MD tracks revenue against plan every month and intervenes early on shortfalls, protecting the annual target.

1.7  Validate revenue history and targets against finance and CRM data.
     ↳  Intended Result:  MD ensures targets are evidence-based and reconciled to NAV/CRM, giving the board credible numbers.

1.8  Align product and pricing strategy to revenue diversification.
     ↳  Intended Result:  MD ensures the product and pricing mix actively supports recurring and international revenue goals.

strategic_theme_alignment: Operational Excellence  (Aligns to Corporate SO17 – Increase Profit)
intended_result: Disciplined profitability management — gross-margin optimisation, value-based pricing, SG&A discipline and prioritisation of high-margin products — that expands margins and aligns the whole organisation toward profitable, high-value growth.
key_initiatives:
2.1  Drive gross-margin optimisation per product line.
     ↳  Intended Result:  MD reviews product-line margins and acts on under-performers, lifting blended gross margin each quarter.

2.2  Review and approve a value-based pricing strategy annually.
     ↳  Intended Result:  MD ensures pricing captures the value delivered rather than defaulting to cost-plus, protecting margin.

2.3  Enforce SG&A discipline with overhead bounded as a % of revenue.
     ↳  Intended Result:  MD caps overhead growth relative to revenue, preserving operating leverage as the business scales.

2.4  Prioritise high-margin products in incentive and resource allocation.
     ↳  Intended Result:  MD aligns sales incentives and investment to margin, steering effort toward profitable growth.

2.5  Hold the CFO accountable for margin and profitability targets.
     ↳  Intended Result:  MD reviews margin dashboards at EXCO so profitability is actively managed, not merely measured.

2.6  Convert cost-efficiency gains into margin improvement.
     ↳  Intended Result:  MD ensures operational savings drop to the bottom line rather than being silently re-absorbed.

2.7  Govern discounting and deal profitability thresholds.
     ↳  Intended Result:  MD sets approval gates for low-margin deals, protecting profitability discipline across sales.

strategic_objective: 3. Optimise Return on Investment & Capital Governance
strategic_theme_alignment: Operational Excellence  (Aligns to Corporate SO18 – Increase ROI)
intended_result: Rigorous capital governance — product-level P&L tracking, a Board Capital Allocation Committee, disciplined business cases and payback thresholds — enabling informed investment decisions, financial accountability and optimised returns on capital.
key_initiatives:
3.1  Establish dedicated product-level P&L tracking.
     ↳  Intended Result:  MD requires a P&L per product so investment decisions are grounded in real, comparable returns.

3.2  Constitute and chair a Board Capital Allocation Committee.
     ↳  Intended Result:  MD works with the board to govern capital deployment with rigour, transparency and accountability.

3.3  Require an annual business-case review for all major capital expenditure.
     ↳  Intended Result:  MD ensures every major investment is justified, tracked and reviewed against its original case.

3.4  Enforce a five-year payback threshold on capital projects.
     ↳  Intended Result:  MD applies a consistent payback discipline so capital flows only to the strongest-return opportunities.

3.5  Track ROI and ROCE as standing board metrics.
     ↳  Intended Result:  MD tables return metrics each board cycle so capital efficiency stays continuously visible.

3.6  Sequence capital toward the highest-return strategic initiatives.
     ↳  Intended Result:  MD phases capex to maximise return within the available cash envelope, avoiding over-extension.

3.7  Hold owners accountable for delivering business-case returns.
     ↳  Intended Result:  MD reviews realised versus projected returns, closing the accountability loop on every investment.

strategic_theme_alignment: Operational Excellence  (Aligns to Corporate SO15 – Reduce Costs)
intended_result: A cost-optimised, well-governed financial operating model — zero-based budgeting, supplier consolidation, a shared-services model and cloud-cost optimisation — that strengthens procurement control and enables sustainable margin improvement and competitive pricing.
key_initiatives:
4.1  Mandate an annual zero-based budgeting exercise.
     ↳  Intended Result:  MD requires every cost to be justified from zero each year, systematically eliminating legacy waste.

4.2  Drive a supplier-consolidation and renegotiation programme.
     ↳  Intended Result:  MD consolidates spend to fewer, better-priced suppliers, improving terms, control and leverage.

4.3  Implement a shared-services model for back-office functions.
     ↳  Intended Result:  MD centralises support functions to cut duplication and lower unit cost as Green scales across markets.

4.4  Establish a procurement framework with formal controls.
     ↳  Intended Result:  MD institutes procurement governance so all spend is controlled, competitive and compliant.

4.5  Launch a cloud-cost-optimisation programme.
     ↳  Intended Result:  MD tracks and optimises cloud spend so infrastructure cost scales efficiently with actual usage.

4.6  Set, monitor and drive down the cost-to-revenue ratio.
     ↳  Intended Result:  MD reviews the cost ratio quarterly, steering it toward the < 55% target by 2029.

4.7  Hold EXCO accountable for cost-efficiency improvements.
     ↳  Intended Result:  MD makes efficiency a shared leadership target, embedding cost discipline into the culture.

strategic_objective: 5. Secure Capital Investment & a Sustainable Funding Engine
strategic_theme_alignment: Operational Excellence  |  Future-Ready Innovation  (Aligns to Corporate SO19 – Increase Capital Investment)
intended_result: A strong, sustainable capital and innovation engine — DFI engagement, a retained-earnings reinvestment policy, asset-financing facilities, ring-fenced R&D and a strategic equity-partner pathway — that funds disciplined reinvestment and long-term growth without over-gearing the balance sheet.
key_initiatives:
5.1  Lead a Development Finance engagement programme (DBN, AfDB, IFC).
     ↳  Intended Result:  MD personally drives development-finance relationships to unlock strategic, patient growth funding.

5.2  Adopt a retained-earnings reinvestment policy (≈ 40% of net profit).
     ↳  Intended Result:  MD secures board approval for disciplined reinvestment, funding growth from internally generated cash.

5.3  Establish an asset-financing facility for regional print-business scaling.
     ↳  Intended Result:  MD arranges financing so the recurring print business can scale regionally without straining capital.

5.4  Ring-fence the R&D budget at 8–10% of revenue.
     ↳  Intended Result:  MD protects R&D funding through the budget cycle so product innovation continues even under pressure.

5.5  Evaluate a strategic equity partner in years three to four.
     ↳  Intended Result:  MD prepares Green for institutional investment by building the governance and track record investors require.

5.6  Maintain a conservative debt-to-equity ratio (below 0.5).
     ↳  Intended Result:  MD governs gearing so the balance sheet stays resilient throughout the expansion programme.

5.7  Present the capital and funding plan to the board for approval.
     ↳  Intended Result:  MD secures board endorsement of the funding strategy, aligning capital firmly to the growth plan.

strategic_objective: 6. Deliver Outstanding Stakeholder Satisfaction & Service Excellence
strategic_theme_alignment: Business Growth & Strategic Partnership  (Aligns to Corporate SO10 – Improve Stakeholder Satisfaction)
intended_result: A high-touch, stakeholder-centric engagement model — account ownership, structured onboarding, 24/7 multilingual support and continuous feedback — that drives strong relationships, rising satisfaction scores and long-term retention across all segments.
key_initiatives:
6.1  Assign a Customer Success / Account Executive to every enterprise account.
     ↳  Intended Result:  MD mandates account ownership so every major client has a single, accountable relationship owner.

6.2  Establish structured stakeholder onboarding programmes.
     ↳  Intended Result:  MD requires a consistent onboarding standard so clients realise value quickly and start strong.

6.3  Institute quarterly satisfaction reviews and an annual NPS programme.
     ↳  Intended Result:  MD reviews NPS/CSAT trends and acts on detractors, making satisfaction a managed strategic metric.

6.4  Stand up a 24/7 multilingual support desk with published SLAs.
     ↳  Intended Result:  MD resources round-the-clock support so Green can credibly serve multiple time zones and markets.

6.5  Centralise and manage all SLAs through the CRM.
     ↳  Intended Result:  MD requires SLA tracking in CRM so adherence is visible, enforceable and reportable.

6.6  Convene a Client Advisory Board twice a year.
     ↳  Intended Result:  MD personally engages top clients for strategic feedback, strengthening loyalty and product direction.

6.7  Hold the COO accountable for satisfaction and SLA outcomes.
     ↳  Intended Result:  MD makes service metrics a standing EXCO item so service excellence is continuously owned.

6.8  Drive rapid Priority-1 incident resolution and root-cause discipline.
     ↳  Intended Result:  MD sets the four-hour P1 standard and reviews every breach, protecting client trust.

7.4  Secure OEM agreements (Dell, HP, Cisco, AWS, Microsoft).

7.7  Secure professional-body memberships across key disciplines.

7.8  Review partner contribution and satisfaction at EXCO.
     ↳  Intended Result:  MD tracks partner revenue and health so under-performing partnerships are addressed promptly.

strategic_objective: 11. Achieve Operational Excellence through Standardised, Automated Processes
strategic_theme_alignment: Operational Excellence  (Aligns to Corporate SO6 – Operational Efficiency)
intended_result: An integrated, automated operating model with fully documented, enforced and digitised core processes, Green's own ERP/PMS deployed internally, and real-time delivery visibility — the efficiency and scalability required to grow globally without proportional cost growth.
key_initiatives:
11.1  Mandate documentation, approval and digitisation of all core processes.

11.2  Champion internal deployment of Green's own ERP and PMS.
     ↳  Intended Result:  MD requires Green to run on its own products, improving them and creating powerful client reference cases.

11.3  Drive a back-office process-automation programme.
     ↳  Intended Result:  MD prioritises automation of repetitive functions, freeing capacity and lowering unit cost as volume scales.

11.4  Commission and resource the ISO 9001 quality-management system.
     ↳  Intended Result:  MD sponsors ISO 9001 implementation so quality is systematised ahead of major international contracts.

11.5  Adopt a stage-gate project-delivery framework enterprise-wide.
     ↳  Intended Result:  MD enforces stage-gate discipline so projects deliver on time and on quality, lifting on-time delivery.

11.6  Hold the COO accountable for delivery and efficiency metrics.
     ↳  Intended Result:  MD reviews delivery and efficiency dashboards at EXCO, embedding operational accountability.

11.7  Deploy real-time operational reporting and PMO oversight.
     ↳  Intended Result:  MD requires a single source of delivery truth so issues are surfaced and resolved early.

11.8  Institutionalise continuous-improvement (lessons-learned) reviews.
     ↳  Intended Result:  MD mandates post-project reviews so process improvements compound over time across the business.

     ↳  Intended Result:  MD drives marketplace onboarding to unlock a global, low-cost distribution and discovery channel.

18.6  Set and review a product-commercialisation pipeline (4 → 6 → 13).
     ↳  Intended Result:  MD tracks the live-product count quarterly, holding the CTIO to the commercialisation schedule.

18.7  Govern a stage-gate product-development and launch process.
     ↳  Intended Result:  MD enforces stage-gates so only market-ready, quality-assured products launch, protecting brand and revenue.

18.8  Tie product investment to recurring-revenue and SaaS-mix targets.
     ↳  Intended Result:  MD allocates product investment toward the highest recurring-revenue potential, accelerating the SaaS shift.

strategic_objective: 19. Build Sovereign, Scalable Strategic ICT Infrastructure
strategic_theme_alignment: Future-Ready Innovation  (Aligns to Corporate SO5 – Increase & Improve Infrastructure)
intended_result: A secure, scalable digital foundation — Data Centre, 24/7 Security Operations Centre, trusted PKI digital-identity services and a live global e-commerce channel — that both underpins product delivery and generates accessible, recurring managed-services revenue.
key_initiatives:
19.1  Secure board approval and financing for the Data Centre build.
     ↳  Intended Result:  MD presents the business case and capital plan to the board, unlocking funding for a strategic asset.

19.2  Drive Data Centre design, build and commissioning to schedule.
     ↳  Intended Result:  MD holds the CTIO to milestone dates and reviews progress quarterly, keeping the build on track.

19.3  Recruit, deploy and commercialise the Security Operations Centre (SOC).
     ↳  Intended Result:  MD resources SOC staffing and go-to-market so it begins signing managed-security clients within the year.

19.4  Architect and launch the PKI / digital-identity service.
     ↳  Intended Result:  MD champions PKI commercialisation, opening a trusted-identity revenue line for regulated clients.

19.5  Launch the e-commerce self-service platform.
     ↳  Intended Result:  MD prioritises a live e-commerce channel so Green can sell and onboard internationally at low fixed cost.

19.6  Position infrastructure as both delivery backbone and revenue source.
     ↳  Intended Result:  MD frames the Data Centre, SOC and PKI as profit centres, ensuring each carries a commercial mandate.

19.7  Establish infrastructure SLAs, security and uptime governance.
     ↳  Intended Result:  MD requires institutional-grade SLAs and controls so infrastructure can serve governments and regulated industries.

19.8  Sequence infrastructure investment within the capital plan.
     ↳  Intended Result:  MD phases infrastructure capex against cash generation and payback thresholds, protecting the balance sheet.
